summary.headline: Happy Forgings Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% to Rs.449 crore and PAT 39.2% to Rs.91 crore, with EBITDA margin at 31.3%.
summary.overview: Record quarterly revenue and profit, driven by 23.1% volume growth and 3.2% higher realisations to Rs.253/kg. EBITDA rose 39.3% to Rs.141 crore, margin up about 275 bps YoY, the fourth straight quarter above 30%. Management says customer price revisions are partly in Q1 (about 30%) and will fully reflect from Q2. Exports were hit by transit delays, with the domestic CV business up about 18%.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles
segments.commentary: 33% of revenue; single-digit growth overall (about 7% per analyst math). Domestic up about 18%; exports down about 12% due to DDP shipments delayed about a month by geopolitical transit issues. CV export share about 7% of revenue.

segments.name: Farm equipment
segments.commentary: 32% of revenue; grew mid-20s. Domestic up over 20%; exports grew despite weak US and Europe tractor demand. Export share about 5% of revenue.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: 16% of revenue; around 50% growth in both domestic and export. Export share about 9% of revenue. Drivers cited: power generation, wind, railways, oil and gas, digital infrastructure.

segments.name: Off-highway
segments.commentary: 11% of revenue; over 40% growth in both domestic and export. Domestic construction equipment up about 9%. Export share about 5% of revenue.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: About 8% of revenue; growth over 70%, domestic over 40%, exports more than doubled as earlier-secured orders began executing. Export share about 8% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth trajectory hold across industrial, export and PV, and can the high gross and EBITDA margins sustain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to strength across CV, farm, PV; a ~Rs.950 crore order book; and new high-realisation products. It said the last price increase was three years ago, supporting margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the price-revision benefit flow from Q2, and is it permanent?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% came in Q1. Domestic: 2% taken in Q1 versus 4.5-5% total, with OEMs passing on from Q2. Increases are on a three-year-old base and described as permanent; currency gains supported exports.

qa_highlights.question: Will solar benefit come in Q4 FY27 and can margins stay above 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar expected on stream from January, with some generation in Q4 and connection through April. Management is confident of upwards of 30% EBITDA margin, citing a 1-1.5% power benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CV revenue grow only ~7% against ~10% industry production growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic CV grew ~18% against ~10% production growth; exports fell ~12% because DDP contracts (Europe, Turkey) saw about a month of deliveries delayed by transit issues.

qa_highlights.question: What is the freight cost impact and recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Container costs rose from about USD 2,000 to USD 6,000. About 75% of contracts are pass-through; company expects a 15-20% hit and is negotiating recovery of about USD 4,500 per container.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export mix by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximate export share of revenue: CV ~7%, PV ~8%, farm ~5%, off-highway ~5%, industrial ~9%.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the Rs.950 crore order book and the Rs.650 crore capex, and plant-level margins for the new industrial line?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book roughly 35-40% industrial, 25-30% PV, 25-30% CV, rest off-highway/farm; 60% export, 40% domestic. New heavy-line gross margins expected around 60-65% with EBITDA about 50% of gross; plant-level margins not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: receivable and inventory days as of June 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days improved with no big change; inventory days about 50 as of date; overall working-capital days improved.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 guidance be revised given strong Q1 volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is high-teen volume growth and it should perform better than that, without giving a revised number.

qa_highlights.question: Asset turns and high base in PV and CV as capex comes on stream in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not worried about a temporary six-month to one-year dip in asset turns, since capacity is being built for future growth; PV growth is from two to three customers with customer acquisition ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Inorganic plans and funding of growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Open to acquisitions and JVs, mainly for technology in energy and aerospace; cautious on expensive valuations in farm/CV. Growth to be funded largely by internal accruals, possibly with a one-year bridge loan for LCs.

guidance_outlook: FY27: expects high-teen volume growth for the year, with EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26 levels and potential for further improvement.

Customer price revisions with OEMs negotiated; about 30% reflected in Q1 and full benefit expected from Q2 onwards. Domestic: roughly 2% taken in Q1 on the ~Rs.100 crore domestic base, with 4.5-5% total taken; described as permanent, from the last base settled about three years ago.

Captive solar power: expected on stream from January 2027 with some generation from Q4 FY27; full connection by April. Management cites a 1-1.5% margin benefit from power; expects EBITDA margin upwards of 30% going forward.

Freight: container rates up from about USD 2,000 to about USD 6,000; around 75% of contracts pass-through, with company expecting a 15-20% hit on the incremental cost and hoping to recover about USD 4,500 from customers.
Heavy-forging/industrial line: management targets industrial revenue doubling in three to four years and PV at 12-15% of revenue; industrial plus PV together to reach about 45-50% of revenue.

Said the new heavy-line business should contribute meaningfully from FY29; new capex to start contributing from Q3-Q4 FY28; capex funded mainly from internal accruals with possibly a one-year bridge loan for LCs.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27: commissioned a 4,000-ton forging press line (4,000 tons added) and 7,200 MT of machining capacity. Total forging capacity 1,52,000 MT; machining capacity 75,200 MT.
Capacity utilisation Q1 FY27: 59% forging, 78% machining.
14,000-ton press line about 65-70% utilised across industrial and CV; a 10,000-ton press line added in Q4 FY26 gives around 30% open capacity by shifting parts.
18,000-ton vertical upsetter line under commissioning; additions from Q4 FY27, trials from Q3 FY27.

Rs.650 crore capex programme referenced by an analyst; management says annual capex of about Rs.350-400 crore and new heavy-line plant (up to 3 ton parts) is being readied at a site, with business from FY29; the new line is about 1.5-3 years from LC opening to production.
Captive solar: capex largely done, clearances obtained, right-of-way work pending.
demand_pricing: Revenue Rs.449 crore (+27%), volumes +23.1%, realisation Rs.253/kg (+3.2%).
CV: domestic +18% on domestic CV production up ~10%; exports down ~12% due to DDP shipments delayed about a month by geopolitical transit issues and higher inventory in transit.
Farm equipment: mid-20s growth; domestic over 20%; exports growing despite weak US and Europe tractor demand.
Industrial: ~50% growth in domestic and export; drivers are power generation, wind, railways, oil and gas, data centres.
Off-highway: over 40% growth; domestic construction equipment ~9%.
Passenger vehicles: over 70% growth, domestic over 40%, exports more than doubled; business concentrated in two to three customers.

Order book ~Rs.950 crore of peak incremental annual revenue over two to three years; split approx. 35-40% industrial, 25-30% PV, 25-30% CV, remainder off-highway and farm; ~60% exports, ~40% domestic. Europe ~60% of exports.
Inventory days about 50 as of June 2026; receivable days improved; overall working capital days improved.
risks_watch: Export execution: DDP delivery delays from geopolitical transit issues and container costs (USD 2,000 to 6,000); 15-20% freight cost hit pending customer recovery.
Timing of price-revision flow: only ~30% in Q1; full benefit from Q2 depends on OEM pass-through; domestic price increase only 2% in Q1 versus 4.5-5% target.
Margin sustainability: EBITDA margin at 31.3% is among the highest in the sector; new capacity and mix shift may lower asset turns through the next 6-12 months per management.
Solar commissioning slipping: management says power from January with full connection by April; any delay pushes the 1-1.5% margin benefit out of FY27.
Passenger vehicle concentration: growth is from two to three customers; high base in PV and CV in H2 FY27.
Capex execution: heavy-line and 18,000-ton upsetter ramp-up timelines (trials Q3, additions Q4 FY27); heavy-line revenue expected only from FY29.
key_quotes: We have now successfully negotiated price revisions with OEMs and benefits from these revisions are expected to fully reflect in our P&L from Quarter 2 onwards.
We continue to expect the business to deliver high teen volume growth during the year while maintaining EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY 26 levels, with potential for further improvement.
As of now, it looks like that we should be able to fund this growth on our own.
I'm not worried about the temporary, you know, six months or one -year kind of a low asset turn because these are the assets which are built for the future.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, margins and the Rs.950 crore order book, with specific targets for FY27 and beyond. Cautious on export timing (transit delays) and on the timing of price-revision flow into Q2.
